what: Federal Signal makes specialist work vehicles and safety equipment. Its products include street sweepers, sewer cleaning trucks, vacuum excavators, road marking equipment and industrial vacuum loaders, plus warning lights and sirens for emergency vehicles and plant alarm systems.
customers: Municipalities, utility contractors, waste and industrial service companies, and emergency services, mostly in North America, bought through dealers and direct contracts.
money: Street sweepers, sewer cleaners, vacuum excavators, dump bodies and road marking equipment.
Emergency vehicle lighting and sirens, industrial warning systems and public alert sirens.
moat: These are specialised machines sold into a dealer network that also services them, and municipal buyers standardise on a brand because their mechanics know it. Replacement cycles are long but predictable, and the aftermarket for parts and service on a large installed base is steady and high-margin.
risks: Municipal budgets fund much of the demand, and those budgets tighten when local tax revenue falls.
The shares trade at about 23 times earnings and 14 times EV/EBITDA, a full price for an equipment maker.
Growth has been helped by acquisitions, which adds integration risk and goodwill.
Debt of $596.1M against $63.7M of cash is modest but the cash cushion is thin.
Utility contractor demand depends on infrastructure spending programmes that have finite funding periods.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $1.2B in 2021 to $2.2B in 2025.
Aftermarket parts and service revenue is recurring and grows with the installed base, which smooths the equipment cycle.
Free cash flow of $365.1M exceeds net income of $296.9M, a sign of genuine cash generation.
Water and sewer infrastructure in the United States is old and requires continuous maintenance, which drives demand for sewer cleaning and vacuum excavation equipment.
watch: Order intake and backlog. Municipal and contractor equipment orders are placed well ahead of delivery, so the backlog shows whether the growth record is continuing.
